capabilities.title: Memory core foundation
capabilities.behavior: Establishes the independent store, shared-contract adapters, schema fence, transaction primitives, scope cursors, and owner-or-exact-grant authorization used by interactive and maintenance writes.
acceptance: Schema, transaction, revision-precondition, and cursor primitives fail atomically with shared errors.
A background worker cannot mutate another project merely because it is a maintenance process or workspace member.

capabilities.title: Authoritative memory records
capabilities.behavior: Stores facts, episodes, notes, conditional smart notes, immutable chronological anchors, and revisable summaries with optimistic mutations and exact raw-source recovery.
acceptance: Concurrent updates using one expected revision produce one commit and one conflict without partial state.
Exact source recovery survives summary publication, and summary decay cannot alter anchor content or provenance.

capabilities.title: Provenance, lineage, and invalidation
capabilities.behavior: Preserves revision ancestry, source spans, verification history, contradiction groups, tombstones, acyclic lineage, and deterministic invalidation of derived state.
acceptance: Editing or tombstoning a source makes stale FTS, vector, rank, and derived-summary rows unreadable in the same transaction.
Lineage cycles and retention-early purges fail while tombstones and competing evidence remain queryable.

capabilities.title: Multi-mode embeddings
capabilities.behavior: Supports off, local, remote-compatible, and managed-service vectors with active-registration fingerprints, response validation, bounded backfill, failure classes, and lexical degradation.
acceptance: Model substitution, invalid dimensions, non-finite values, zero norm, retired registration, and stale content are refused without replacing valid vectors.
Backfills stop and checkpoint at item, token, request, retry, cost, or wall-time limits and cool down stalled batches.

capabilities.title: Unified retrieval and ranking
capabilities.behavior: Searches authorized memories, messages, files, and commits using lexical, semantic, or hybrid modes, deterministic score fusion, date filters, visible-content suppression, and bounded reranking.
acceptance: Unauthorized, expired, tombstoned, stale, and already-visible candidates cannot leak through any search mode.
Stable results expose source, provenance, verification, contradiction, score components, suppression counts, and Cursor.

capabilities.title: Fenced background maintenance
capabilities.behavior: Schedules extraction, verification, smart-note evaluation, summarization, decay, vector work, reconciliation, invalidation, compaction, integrity, portability, and purge with per-scope leases and model budgets.
acceptance: Grant revocation, lease expiry, token mismatch, changed input, or changed configuration prevents stale publication.
Model accounting distinguishes unknown usage from zero and cannot exceed reserved budgets.
Smart-note conditions execute only through the allowlisted bounded predicate interpreter.

capabilities.title: Message, file, and git indexes
capabilities.behavior: Maintains recoverable raw-message indexing, predicate-controlled file indexing, and opt-in bounded git indexing with pre-publication identity and digest checks.
acceptance: Message reconciliation resumes from the earliest durable dirty sequence before advancing its cursor.
File reads cannot publish after symlink escape, policy denial, scope loss, or digest change, and rejected content is not stored.
Git scans publish only against the same repository identity and refs and persist cooldown for non-repositories.

capabilities.title: OSS Gideon clients and modules
capabilities.behavior: Exposes typed record, search, maintenance, diagnostics, and lifecycle clients from runtime/gideon/hypermid without allowing Python to write the core database directly.
acceptance: Python and Rust preserve shared Scope, Cursor, Error, and Trace semantics for success, conflict, authorization failure, and cancellation.
OSS lifecycle startup, health, drain, and shutdown preserve durable work and lexical-only operation.

capabilities.title: Local bus and remote-safe protocol
capabilities.behavior: Provides a versioned, authenticated transport with equivalent in-process and local-bus request, stream, cancellation, backpressure, cursor replay, and mutation-idempotency behavior.
acceptance: Both transports pass the same conformance vectors with equivalent records, errors, traces, cursors, and termination.
Transport identity cannot replace actor Scope, and replay cannot duplicate an acknowledged mutation.

capabilities.title: Staged import and canonical export
capabilities.behavior: Stages and validates versioned imports before visibility and emits digest-covered canonical JSON Lines containing authoritative records and provenance without derivative or secret-bearing state.
acceptance: Import replay is idempotent by source digest and item key, with rejected items inspectable and no partial batch visibility.
Scope relocation requires destination write authority, and export excludes vectors, indexes, leases, jobs, credentials, and secret references.

capabilities.title: Migration and recovery
capabilities.behavior: Fences unsupported stores, journals transactional migrations, creates consistent backups, validates authoritative graphs, and rebuilds derivative state through the OSS Gideon lifecycle.
acceptance: Newer unsupported schemas fail closed and destructive migration requires a verified backup manifest.
Fresh and migrated schemas converge, and repair preserves authoritative revisions while rebuilding only derivative state.
The first complete integration runs locally in OSS Gideon without a hosted dependency or rollout.

capabilities.title: OSS release integration
capabilities.behavior: Packages the complete local memory slice with lifecycle wiring, compatibility gates, and content-safe diagnostics, with no hosted rollout or hosted dependency.
acceptance: A clean OSS profile creates, retrieves, maintains, exports, restores, and re-retrieves the same authoritative records through Python and Rust.
Diagnostics cover schema, indexes, vectors, queues, leases, budgets, and recovery without exposing memory content or secrets.
